ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A light spring is fixed at the upper end, and a small ball with mass $m=0.1\mathrm{kg}$ is attached to the lower end. When the ball is at rest, the spring elongation is $10\mathrm{cm}$. The ball is now set into simple harmonic motion in the vertical direction. Timing begins when the ball is released from the lowest point. The displacement $y$ of the ball relative to the equilibrium position as a function of time $t$ is shown in Figure 2. The gravitational acceleration $g$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. What is the expression for the displacement of the small ball relative to its equilibrium position as a function of time?
2. Find the total distance traveled by the small ball within the time interval of $0{\sim}12.9\mathrm{s}$.
3. When the small ball reaches the highest point, the elongation of the spring is $5\mathrm{cm}$. What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the ball at this moment?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: Figure 1 on the left side of the figure is a vertical light spring with the upper end fixed, and the lower end connected to a small ball. Figure 2 on the right side is the displacement-time graph of the small ball relative to the equilibrium position, with the vertical axis labeled y/cm and the horizontal axis labeled t/s; the curve is at y=+5 cm when t=0, then is at y=-5 cm when t=0.6 s, and then returns to y=+5 cm when t=1.2 s. Therefore, from the graph, the amplitude A=5 cm and the period T=1.2 s are read. Then reason: timing starts from the release of the small ball at the lowest point, and the initial point in the graph corresponds to y=+5 cm, so the displacement can be written in cosine form: y=A cos(ωt). The angular frequency ω=2π/T=2π/1.2=5π/3 rad/s, therefore y=5 cos(5πt/3) cm. Within 0 to 12.9 s, 12.9 s=10×1.2 s+0.9 s, that is, it includes 10 complete periods plus 0.9 s. In each complete period, the distance traveled by the small ball is 4A=4×5 cm=20 cm, and the distance for 10 periods is 200 cm. In the remaining 0.9 s, starting from the phase y=+5 cm, in the first 0.6 s it reaches y=-5 cm, with distance 10 cm; after another 0.3 s it reaches the equilibrium position y=0, with distance 5 cm. Therefore the remaining part of the distance is 15 cm, and the total distance is 200 cm+15 cm=215 cm=2.15 m. When the small ball is in static equilibrium, the spring is stretched by 10 cm, and mg=kx0, so k=mg/0.10=(0.1×10)/0.10=10 N/m. At the highest point, the spring is stretched by 5 cm, the magnitude of the spring force is k×0.05=10×0.05=0.5 N, the magnitude of gravity is mg=1.0 N, and the magnitude of the resultant force is 1.0-0.5=0.5 N. The magnitude of the acceleration is a=F/m=0.5/0.1=5 m/s².
